items.content_html:
Value Prop

The async merge API gives you a single, reliable endpoint for merging any pull request — whether it's a direct merge, merge queue, stacked PR, or unstacked PR. You no longer need to track which endpoint to call for each scenario, and merges run asynchronously so they won't time out on large or complex repositories. This makes automating pull request workflows simpler and more resilient.

Expected Outcome

Developers and teams building on the GitHub API can merge pull requests consistently without hitting the 10-second timeout that affects the existing merge endpoints. By consolidating all merge paths into one endpoint, the API becomes easier to adopt and maintain across different repository configurations. This release moves the async merge API from public preview to general availability, making it the recommended approach for programmatic PR merges.
items.title: Async Merge API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now get AI-powered security findings directly in the code scanning alert backlog alongside your existing CodeQL results — no Actions workflow to set up or maintain, just a single click to enable. AI scanning extends coverage to languages and vulnerability classes that rule-based analysis doesn't reach, so more of your codebase is protected from day one. Findings are deduplicated and reverified automatically, keeping your alert backlog stable, reliable, and low-noise.

Expected Outcome

Developers across every supported language get actionable security coverage without the overhead of configuring or owning a scanning pipeline. By bringing AI-generated findings into the same familiar triage experience as CodeQL alerts, teams can act on a broader set of vulnerabilities without changing how they work. The public preview gives GitHub Advanced Security customers an early path to a more complete and trustworthy security signal across their repositories.
items.title: Code Scanning: full-repo AI scans [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

The global search bar in GitHub navigation now runs on a modern React foundation, giving logged-in users a search experience that looks and feels exactly as before — with no disruption to their workflow. This update brings the search bar into GitHub's unified UI service, enabling faster iteration and richer search capabilities in the future. Developers can continue searching GitHub the same way they always have, with a more reliable and maintainable experience under the hood.

Expected Outcome

Migrating QuickSearch to React consolidates GitHub's global navigation into a single, modern UI framework, removing the complexity of maintaining separate UI stacks. This foundation unblocks the team's ability to build and ship navigation and search improvements more quickly going forward. The outcome is a more consistent, evolvable experience for developers who rely on GitHub's global search every day.
items.title: React-based Quick Search [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Start a session from anywhere in GitHub Mobile—whether you're viewing an issue, pull request, or Actions log—and get a consistent, sandbox-first experience every time. Your repository and relevant context automatically carry over, so you can get to work without extra setup steps.

Expected Outcome

We're standardizing how sessions start across GitHub Mobile to eliminate confusion about where code runs and reduce friction in your workflow. This gives you one predictable way to begin a session from any part of the app, making GitHub Codespaces the clear default while preserving the specific context you need.
items.title: GitHub Mobile: Replace mobile session entry points with the sandbox creation experience [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Enterprise admins can now look up which cost center any user, organization, repository, or team belongs to with a single REST API call—no more scanning through entire cost center lists to find where a resource's usage is charged. This makes billing automation and cost tracking straightforward and efficient.

Expected Outcome

By providing a direct lookup endpoint, enterprises can build accurate billing systems that automatically route usage charges to the correct cost center and give their finance teams visibility into resource costs without manual reconciliation or exhaustive API scans.
items.title: Look up which cost center a resource belongs to via the REST API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GitHub Apps now support enterprise and organization management APIs—including settings, delegated policies, domain verification, two-factor authentication, and bypass requests—letting you retire classic personal access tokens and adopt least-privilege automation. You get more control, better security, and full parity with classic PAT capabilities for enterprise-scale operations.

Expected Outcome

This release helps enterprises and organizations transition away from classic personal access tokens entirely, enabling them to implement stricter security policies and automate administrative workflows using the more secure GitHub Apps authentication model. By filling these API gaps, teams can now standardize on GitHub Apps across their entire automation stack without compromise.
items.title: More Enterprise APIs support GitHub Apps (org/repo settings, enterprise profile, delegated bypass requests) [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Pin your important Copilot sessions and projects on mobile to keep your most-used work front and center. Instead of scrolling through your Copilot feed to find what matters, pinned items stay at the top where you can access them instantly, whether you're on iOS or Android.

Expected Outcome

As teams juggle more sessions and projects, we want to make it easier for you to organize your workflow on mobile. By letting you curate your Copilot tab with pinned items, we're reducing the friction of finding your active work so you can stay focused and productive on the go.
items.title: GitHub Mobile: Pin important Copilot sessions and projects [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Quickly find and focus on the sessions you need in GitHub Copilot Home by organizing them with custom filters and grouping options. Whether you want to see sessions by repository, environment, agent type, or status, you now have the control to reduce clutter and speed up your workflow.

Expected Outcome

As teams accumulate more Copilot sessions across different projects and environments, staying organized becomes critical. This feature gives users the ability to tailor their Copilot Home feed to match their workflow, making it easier to locate active work, spot sessions that need attention, and maintain productivity across multiple coding contexts.
items.title: GitHub Mobile: Configure the Copilot Home feed [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Stop resetting your whitespace preference every time you review a pull request. Save a personal default to hide whitespace changes across all your future reviews, and override it whenever you need to see the full diff. This keeps formatting changes from cluttering your review and lets you focus on what actually matters in the code.

Expected Outcome

Reviewers spend less time configuring the same preference on repeat and get clearer visibility into substantive code changes. Pull request diffs stay accurate—file, addition, and deletion counts align with the filtered view—and users get a clear warning before hiding whitespace in file types where it could mask meaningful behavior changes.
items.title: Remember Whitespace Visibility Preference Across Pull Requests [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Enterprise administrators can now confidently install third-party GitHub Apps across their organization with the security and support of a generally available feature. This gives teams access to a growing ecosystem of integrations that extend GitHub's capabilities while maintaining enterprise-grade governance and control.

Expected Outcome

We're marking Enterprise Installed GitHub Apps as GA to demonstrate platform maturity and give enterprises the assurance they need to standardize on GitHub App integrations. This removes preview labels and feature flags, establishing this as a stable, production-ready tool that enterprises can rely on for managing applications across their deployments.
items.title: Enterprise Installed GitHub Apps are GA [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Admins can now grant GitHub Apps permission to create repositories without giving them broad repository administration access. This new repository_creation:write permission lets organizations adopt least-privilege security practices, making it safer to authorize integrations.

Expected Outcome

By separating repository creation from full admin permissions, we're removing a barrier that prevents customers from adopting security best practices. Organizations can confidently grant app access for specific capabilities they need without exposing unnecessary risk, and integration partners can serve their users with a more secure permission model.
items.title: Separate "Repo creation" permission supports least-privilege GitHub App usage and allows repo admins easier installation management [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now set your preferred model tier—whether efficiency, balanced, or max—as the default when using auto-tier selection in managed settings. This gives your team or enterprise a consistent performance baseline that matches your specific needs without requiring per-request configuration.

Expected Outcome

We're enabling enterprises and teams to align GitHub Copilot model tier defaults with their organizational preferences and use cases. This reduces friction for teams that want more aggressive performance (max tier) or cost-conscious defaults (efficiency tier) across their managed deployments.
items.title: Set a specific Auto tier as the default via managed settings [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

GHES administrators can now configure AI model providers centrally, allowing developers using Copilot CLI to access AI assistance without routing traffic through GitHub Cloud. This gives enterprises the control and compliance posture they need while maintaining developer productivity.

Expected Outcome

We're extending Copilot CLI support to air-gapped GHES environments, removing the blocker of requiring GitHub Cloud connectivity. This unlocks Copilot usage for GHES customers who have strict network isolation policies, expanding our addressable market within the enterprise segment.
items.title: Copilot in GHES: Allow operators to configure models centrally in GHES for Copilot CLI to use. [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Track how your repository's code coverage evolves over time with a line chart on the overview page. See whether your coverage is trending up with your improvements or down in areas that need attention, with flexible timeframes of 14, 30, or 90 days to match your review cycle.

Expected Outcome

Maintainers gain visibility into coverage trends so they can make informed decisions about where to focus testing efforts and celebrate progress as code quality improves across their repository.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: coverage history on the overview page [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Maintainers can now see code coverage metrics specifically for newly added code, making it easier to track the quality of recent work separate from your overall repository coverage. This visibility helps teams focus on quality standards for the code they're actively developing.

Expected Outcome

By distinguishing new-code coverage from overall repository coverage, teams gain better insight into the quality of their incremental changes. This supports more focused code quality discussions and helps maintainers make better decisions about which areas of development need attention.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: new-code coverage chip [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now see your repository's code coverage at a glance with our new coverage overview. The feature displays your current default-branch line coverage so you know exactly how well your codebase is tested, giving your team a clear picture of your testing health.

Expected Outcome

We're building comprehensive repository-level code coverage reporting to help maintainers monitor and improve testing practices. This initial release establishes the foundation with current coverage visibility, with additional coverage insights and tooling coming in future releases.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: current coverage overview in the UI [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Maintainers and integrations can now retrieve current repository code coverage through a supported, stable API and understand exactly which data contributes to that result. This gives you programmatic access to coverage metrics you can integrate directly into your workflows and tools.

Expected Outcome

We're releasing the code coverage API to general availability so teams can confidently build integrations on top of a stable contract. This enables better visibility into code quality trends and helps maintainers make informed decisions about test coverage across their repositories.
items.title: GitHub Code Quality: current default-branch coverage API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now access complete security advisory data directly through the GraphQL API, including fields like cveId, severity, url, and review timestamps. New filter arguments for severity and withdrawal status let you narrow results server-side, so your queries return exactly what you need without extra processing. If your integration is built on GraphQL, you no longer need to maintain a separate REST client just to read advisory information.

Expected Outcome

Developers and security teams who rely on GitHub GraphQL APIs can now build and maintain simpler, more efficient integrations for consuming security advisory data. Closing these gaps between the REST and GraphQL advisory APIs reduces unnecessary complexity, lowers rate-limit pressure, and removes a documented barrier to GraphQL-only workflows. The result is a more consistent API experience across GitHub security tooling.
items.title: More global security advisory data is now available in the GraphQL API [GA]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

Code Quality scanning now works across multiple branches, not just your default branch. You can run scans on protected branches, release branches, or any branch that matters to your team's workflow. This gives you quality insights where and when you need them, regardless of where active development is happening.

Expected Outcome

Extending Code Quality scanning beyond the default branch helps teams catch issues earlier — before they reach main — and enforces consistent quality standards across all critical branches. Teams that rely on protected or long-lived branches gain the same visibility they've come to expect on their default branch, reducing the risk of quality regressions slipping through.
items.title: Multi-branch Code Quality scanning [Public Preview]

items.content_html:
Value Prop

You can now upload code coverage reports in more formats — including Go's native coverage format — directly to GitHub, without converting them first. This removes a manual, error-prone step that affected developers working with Go modules and other test frameworks that don't produce Cobertura XML. Broader format support means your coverage data reaches GitHub accurately, so you get reliable insights into test health across your repositories.

Expected Outcome

Expanding coverage report format support reduces friction for developers whose toolchains generate non-Cobertura output, making it easier to adopt GitHub's code coverage features without workarounds. Go native format support addresses the most-requested gap from public preview feedback, and accurate module path handling eliminates the basename collision issues introduced by third-party converters. The result is more teams getting complete, trustworthy coverage data with less setup effort.
items.title: Code coverage: expanded report format support [GA]
